_comment: Go-vs-Python parity for a ROOT platform file's `tenants:` block (#1982).
Semantics: that block is the platform's per-tenant DEFAULT. The tenant's own
file wins key by key whatever either file is called; a key the tenant file
does not write keeps the platform value; a platform file cannot create a
tenant (no tenant file declares it -> absent on both planes, WARN); a NESTED
platform file's `tenants:` block is read by no plane (exporter WARNs).
Go (config_platform_tenant_overlay_test.go) loads each tree through
NewConfigManager+Load and reads the resolved mysql_connections row (what
/metrics serves); Python (test_platform_tenant_overlay_parity.py) reads the
routing plane, _grar_parse.load_tenant_tree. Neither reads the other's
source; both assert this table.
expect.<tenant>: metric = mysql_connections on /metrics (null = tenant
absent); dedup = routing plane _severity_dedup (null = tenant absent there);
group_wait = routing plane merged group_wait (null = the plane builds no route for it).
exporter_dedup / silent_mode = what the exporter resolves for the tenant
(ResolveSeverityDedup: enable/disable; ResolveSilentModes: sorted target
severities joined by ',', '' = none); null = tenant absent from the exporter.
Go asserts metric/exporter_dedup/silent_mode, Python dedup/group_wait.
The routing plane is flat by design, so a tenant declared only in a
subdirectory has dedup null while it still EXISTS for platform-file purposes.
Measured on main 19dc4c76 before the fix: c1 rows served tx on /metrics;
c3 TX.yaml / 0tx.yaml served 60 (tx.yaml 70); c2-c5 tx.yaml gave dedup
enable (TX.yaml / 0tx.yaml disable).
